mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strengthening economy, boosting consumer and investor confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, leading to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, which in turn boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced output and potential earnings declines.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real personal savings (RSAFS) decrease by more than 5% within the last month, it signals increased consumer spending and confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS decreases > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month, it signals a strong labor market, boosting investor confidence and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate future rate hikes.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% year-over-year and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 2% YoY increase), it signals strong economic growth without inflationary pressure, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% YoY and CPIAUCSL increases < 2% YoY
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
